issue_context.title: Upgrade from 4.13 to 4.14, in typescript, fundamentally changed and breaks core features of data management
comments:
Hello, thanks for opening the issue, happy to try to help you with that.

It seems that populate doesn't understand what fields are returned by `getFullPopulateObject()` and thus doesn't add anything to the final object.

Out of curiosity what's the return type of this method?

ps: Previously they were compatible because they weren't typed at all (`any`)

> This is a templated message

Hello @woodyjon,

I see you are wanting to ask a question that is not really a bug report,

- questions should be directed to [our forum](https://forum.strapi.io) or our [Discord](https://discord.strapi.io)
- feature requests should be directed to our [feedback and feature request database](https://feedback.strapi.io)

Please see the following contributing guidelines for asking a question [here](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-an-issue).

Thank you.

OK, I understand. But everything working fine, then many things not working anymore after an upgrade, I would love some explanation of what was changed and why. I am not the only one who will face those issues after the upgrade, I am guessing.

I'm wondering what improvement could be done to fix things here.

Do you have access to the inferred return type of getFullPopulateObject? I'm trying to understand if it resolves to a wider type or if it keeps a literal object representation of your object.

Also, in the event where there is a value for the populate but it's not recognized by the type handler, I'm wondering if we should interpret that as either "all populatable keys" or "no populatable keys"

```
 error TS2339: Property 'material' does not exist on type 'GetValues<"api::batch.batch", GetNonPopulatableKeys<"api::batch.batch">>'.

548     if (batch.material.pkgType !== PkgType.SS) {
```

```
error TS2339: Property 'flags' does not exist on type 'GetValues<"api::batch.batch", GetNonPopulatableKeys<"api::batch.batch">>'.

490         batch.flags.push(flag);
```

Tells you that the returned entities don't contain the `material` and `flags` attributes.

Based on the definition of you `getFullObjectPopulate`, it looks like those are populatable attributes (**relations**, **components**, **dynamic zones**, or **media**).

Those kinds of fields are dynamically added to the result entities based on your query (`populate`)

If you say `populate: 'material',` you should get the autocomplete for it in the returned entities, same for `flags`. Hence the questions about the return type of the getPopulate method, because based on the given definition, it should work as intended.

>It seems the strapi api now expects types that are like:
>```
>{
>    id: 
>    attributes: {
>        attribute1:
>        attribute2:
>    }
>}

I'm really not sure how you've come to encounter this, attributes shouldn't be part of any internal API, especially not around the entity service.

Thanks. Will try that. Makes sense. The collection extending the Strapi entity is nice.
It still feels a bit a pity that we have to create a different object with a different type to input for create and update. (And that will need a lot of work on my backend ;-))
Cheers.

Just wanted to bump this. Seing your whole strapi-codebase break like that (with a minor version upgrade) and not being able to find any information about it (despite now this thread) is not a pleasant experience. I't be better to only ship such breaking changes when there is a good documentaion and migration guide for it. Apart from that, it's actually nice to see strapi getting better typescript support.

This hasn't been forgotten.

> I would like to help write some guides for the typescript topic. But I think I'm still missing your 'official' way of doing typescript things

Hey, thank you for your interest, we should _soon_ start writing guides on how to work with Strapi types. We are just waiting a bit more to stabilize the APIs and make sure we won't introduce breaking changes after documenting the usage.

> Just wanted to bump this. Seing your whole strapi-codebase break like that (with a minor version upgrade) and not being able to find any information about it (despite now this thread) is not a pleasant experience

I know it can be (very) frustrating, but we had to make a decision at some point in order to move forward with the topic and start improving things. The lack of documentation for this is a serious issue that we have in our backlog. Even though I cannot guarantee a precise ETA, I wanted to guarantee that this is not a topic lost at the bottom of our priorities.

> Apart from that, it's actually nice to see strapi getting better typescript support.

Thanks, really appreciate it.

You have to be a typescript power user and worked with Strapi types before to fully get along with this. I mean just take a look at [the attributes utils file](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/8811cfafd27e6318bde3951dadbe45dfe1acbce3/packages/core/types/src/types/core/attributes/utils.ts) (its minified in the package). It is cool that e.g. the entity service will check for population options, but if the trade off for stuff like that is that I can't let a junior dev make any type changes related to Strapi, then it is not the right way for me.

review_comments:
I'm wondering if renaming OmitRelationsWithoutTarget (as well as moving the export path of it, along with ID and literals) would be considered a breaking change, since we do export it in @strapi/strapi, even though it's not documented.

Could we get around that by also continuing to export them the same way from this file, with a note to remove the dual-export in v5?

Root namespaces are unchanged, which I think should be the way the "types breaking changes" should be looked at.

We should advise people to use root-level namespace imports (`@strapi/strapi`) instead of deep ones (`@strapi/strapi/core/entity-service/...`), which -in my opinion- correspond to the public type API

Hence, since the splitting offers more readability from a maintainer perspective (at least I believe so), I would keep it personally like this. What do you think?
Ok, I agree, I think as long as we keep the namespaces the same people shouldn't be using the deep references.
